# Terraform

Launch uses Terraform to provision resources in Azure for Blob Storage, which is currently used
to store workflow payloads.

Based on the recommendation of the ABS paved path, a separate folder is used per environment.

```
config/terraform/
  lab/
    main.tf
    terraform.tfvars.json
    variables.tf
    versions.tf
  production/
    main.tf
    terraform.tfvars.json
    variables.tf
    versions.tf
...
```

Each environment will have separate resource groups and storage accounts, but could utilize the same
Azure regions (such as Lab & Production, future Proxima stamps in the same region).

Each environment will use multiple storage accounts for redundancy and multiple Azure regions if they're available. Azure [recommends the resource group is in the same location as the resources][azure-rg-location],
so a resource group needs to be created for each Azure region used by the storage accounts.

A map of the Azure region and storage account indexes is stored in `storage_account_regions` TF variable.
```json
{
  "storage_account_regions": {
    "eastus": [0,1,2],
    "eastus2": [3,4,5]
  }
}
```

The storage account name will be generated by our team prefix "launch", the environment/stamp, and that index.
For example, a Lab storage account would have the name `launchlabsa2`. If that storage account was in the `eastus` region, it would live in the `rg-launch-lab-eastus` resource group.

For launch to access these resources, a SPN will be created per environment scoped to all of the resource
groups created in that environment.

[azure-rg-location]: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/overview#what-location-should-i-use-for-my-resource-group

## Deploying

Deployments can be done via comments on a pull request.

1. Get approval for your changes
1. Get the Terraform plan for your changes by commenting `.noop <environment>` on the PR
1. Validate that the changes from the Terraform plan are what you'd expect
1. Apply your changes by commenting `.deploy <environment>` on the PR
1. Deploy your PR by doing through the merge queue.

This is enabled by the [ABS branch deploy workflow](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/152bf365213c5f98497aab0f1fd2d230f00d81cc/.github/workflows/branch-deploy.yml).

See the [branch deploy action](https://github.com/github/branch-deploy#available-commands-) for a
full list of available commands.

## Adding a new stamp

This documents the process to configure Terraform for a new environment to provision any Azure resources (currently just Azure Blob Storage).
The documentation assumes the new environment is a Proxima stamp, so some modifications may be necessary when provisioning a non-Proxima environment.

You'll need to be a member of the [`tfe-launch`](https://github.com/github/entitlements/blob/0dc2246e849616068a69dde9b049be36d779da38/ldap/apps/terraform-enterprise/tfe-launch.txt)
Terraform team and [`azure-actions-launch-contributor`](https://github.com/github/entitlements/blob/0dc2246e849616068a69dde9b049be36d779da38/ldap/apps/azure/azure-actions-launch-contributor.txt)
Azure group to complete most of these steps.

### Create a Terraform Workspace

Follow the [instructions in the ABS paved path documentation to create a new Terraform Workspace](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#workspace)
in the `azure-launch` Terraform Enterprise organization: https://terraform.githubapp.com/app/azure-launch/workspaces.

The workspace name should be `launch-` followed by the Proxima stamp name.

The steps are are summarized here, but validate that nothing has changed in the ABS paved path documentation.

1. Login to Terraform via [Okta](https://github.okta.com/).
1. Navigate to https://terraform.githubapp.com/app/azure-launch/workspaces
1. Click the "New" button in the top-right and then "Workspace" in the top right
1. Select the "Default Project" in the "Create a new workspace" dialog
1. Choose "CLI-Driven Workflow" when prompted to "Choose your workflow"
1. Name the workspace `launch-` followed by the stamp name (ex. `launch-staff-wus2-01` or `launch-prod-weu-01`)
1. Add a description along the lines of "Azure Blob Storage resources for Launch in the [STAMP] Proxima stamp"
1. On the page for the new workspace, click "Settings" in the left sidebar
1. In the main "General" settings page, change the "Terraform Version" to 1.7.0 (this should match [.terraform-version](./.terraform-version))
1. On the same page, under "Execution Mode" ensure it's set to "Organization Default" and verify that the subtext confirms that `remote` is the `azure-launch` organization's default.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7eeeb01-0d6d-414f-9038-0ab2157787b5)
1. Scroll down to the bottom and click "Save settings"

### Determine the appropriate Azure Regions

Consult the [Resiliency Guidance for Proxima documentation](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/main/docs/resilience-guidance.md#resiliency-guidance-for-proxima) for how failover regions should be configured in Proxima.


See [Proxima Azure Data Centers](https://github.com/github/proxima/blob/main/docs/proxima-azure-datacenters.md)
for the primary region for each stamp.

You'll need the Azure CLI abbreviated region name, which can be found under "Azure CLI name" in this
[region mapping list](https://github.com/claranet/terraform-azurerm-regions/blob/master/REGIONS.md)
or via the Azure CLI with `az account list-locations -o table`.

### Add the environment to the Terraform Branch Deploy workflow

The [Terraform Branch Deploy](/.github/workflows/terraform-branch-deploy.yml) workflow includes all of the
valid `environment-targets`.
This needs to be updated to include the new environment.
This workflow runs on `issue_comment` on the default branch, so the new environment needs to be added
and merged *before* any Terraform configuration for that new environment.

### Create Terraform configuration files

A new directory in [`config/terraform`](https://github.com/github/launch/tree/main/config/terraform) should be created for each environment.
The configuration files should be copied from an existing directory:
1. Use `config/terraform/prod-weu-01` as a template for a Proxima environment
1. Use `config/terraform/production` as a template for a non-Proxima environment

The `terraform.tfvars.json` file should be updated to use the Proxima region(s) chosen previously.
For each region, it's recommended that three storage accounts are created:

```json
{
  "storage_account_regions": {
    "region1": [0,1,2],
    "region2": [3,4,5]
  }
}
```

The `main.tf` file should be updated to reference the name of the workspace created for this environment
and the `stamp` local variable.

The SPN used by TF is in Launch's production vault, so `vault_environment` can be left as `production`.

The Terraform file will use these variables to create a resource group per region and a storage account
for each number.

For the above example, assuming an environment named `prod-example-01`,
a resource group `rg-launch-prod-example-01-region1` will be created in `region1` with storage accounts
`launchproxexample01sa0`, `launchproxexample01sa1`, and `launchproxexample01sa2`.
A second resource group `rg-launch-prod-example-01-region2` will be created in `region2` with storage accounts
`launchproxexample01sa3`, `launchproxexample01sa4`, and `launchproxexample01sa5`.

Storage account names must be unique and will only include the environment name and *not* the region name,
so ensure each number referenced in an environment is not already used in a different region's list
of storage account.

### Validate and Deploy Changes

Create a pull request with the Terraform configuration changes and follow the steps in [Deploying](#deploying)
to plan and apply the Terraform configuration.

Once provisioned, the resources can be viewed in the Azure Portal with your `@githubazure.com` account.

[GitHub - Prod - Actions - Launch | Resource Groups](https://portal.azure.com/#@githubazure.onmicrosoft.com/resource/subscriptions/380b7bd4-a93e-4619-a732-ee564febbf46/resourceGroups)


### Create an SPN for the environment

Per the [paved path best practices](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#one-service-principal-per-environment-with-restricted-permissions),
each environment should have its own SPN scoped to the `Storage Blob Data Contributor` role and
the resource groups in that environment.

This SPN is used by Launch to interact with blob storage and is separate from the all access SPN used
by Terraform to manage resources.

In `github/azure-rbac`, clone one of the Proxima-related `.tf` files [under `tf/rbac/` with the naming convention `spn-launch-blob-<stamp-name>.tf`](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Agithub%2Fazure-rbac++path%3Atf%2Frbac%2Fspn-launch-blob*.tf&type=code).

This should be copied from an existing Launch SPN from an another environment and modified to set the
appropriate `display_name`, `vault_env` and `resource_group`. `resource_group` should match the resource group
created by Terraform.

```tf
module "spn-launch-blob-<stamp>" {
  source = "./modules/service_principal"

  display_name = "spn-launch-blob-<stamp>"
  catalog_service = "launch"
  vault_app = "launch"
  vault_env = "<stamp>"

  tags = [
    "autocred"
  ]

  providers = {
    azuread = azuread
    azurerm = azurerm
  }

  access = [
    {
      role              = "Storage Blob Data Contributor",
      subscription_path = module.actions-launch.subscription_path,
      resource_group    = "rg-launch-<stamp-><region>",
    }
  ]
}
```

[Example SPN for `prod-sdc-01`](https://github.com/github/azure-rbac/blob/a4cfd0f71b993a7dbb303c51acb756009b99723f/tf/rbac/spn-launch-blob-prod-sdc-01.tf)


See https://github.com/github/azure-rbac/pull/2549 for an example PR and the paved path documentation linked above for more details.

>[!NOTE]
>Every SPN should have a unique SPN `display_name` to help differentiate them.
>The `lab`, `dotcom`, `staff-wus2-01`, and `prod-weu-01` all use the same display name, but new SPNs
>should not follow that pattern.
>This `display_name` will also affect the name used by the Azure RBAC automation to store the SPN in Launch's vault
### Set up Private Link

Private Link is required for Proxima environments.

As documented in [ABS Paved Path: Proxima Networking](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/main/docs/networking.md#proxima),
two Private Endpoint configurations are necessary:

1. In `eastus` for the Terraform Enterprise runners - https://github.com/github/sites/pull/1370
2. In the Proxima site/region for access from Launch - https://github.com/github/sites/pull/1368

Without the first private endpoint, Terraform plans updating or modifying the storage accounts after they've
been created will fail due to `allow_gh_dcs` being disabled in Proxima environments on the storage accounts.

Follow the above examples and refer to the paved path documentation for full details.

After the Terraform plan is applied to the `eastus` and Proxima `site`, you'll need JIT access
to the `azure-launch` subscription to manually approve the connection on each storage account.
See [approving the connection](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/17840ed8481113b35426ac03120443d56154e2e7/docs/networking.md#approving-the-connection).

### Add Launch configuration

The following values are required by [`BlobConfig`](https://github.com/github/launch/blob/25345e64a6552773a9f516bc2efac5f598c7fed6/clients/launchblob/blob.go#L15-L25)
1. `AZURE_SPN_CLIENT_SECRET` - `spn_launch_blob_<stamp_with_underscores>` in Vault
1. `AZURE_SPN_CLIENT_ID` - `spn_launch_blob_<stamp_with_underscores>_client_id` in Vault
1. `AZURE_SPN_TENANT_ID` - `spn_launch_blob_<stamp_with_underscores>_tenant_id` in Vault
1. `AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_PREFIX` - configured in the Terraform file using the stamp name without any hyphens.
1. `AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME` (optional) - configured in the Terraform file via `storage_container_names`. This should only be set if using a container name other than the default of `payloads`.
1. `AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_COUNT` (optional) - the number of storage accounts across all regions in the stamp. This only needs to be set if the default of 3 is not being used.

See https://github.com/github/launch/pull/8230 for an example of setting this configuration.

## DNS

If a *non-Proxima* environment is being added, DNS might be required so that requests from GitHub
Data Centers are routed through the Private Links.

This is also necessary if additional `lab` or `production` storage accounts are introduced.

See [ABS Networking](https://github.com/github/ABS/blob/e6a6d79f65d2501c08a69a878e23fcd0735bc39c/docs/networking.md#privatelink)
for more details and [this pull request](https://github.com/github/puppet/pull/37100) which added
the DNS entries for the `lab` and `production` storage accounts.
